text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- About 55 percent of Norwegian companies have ignored an instruction from authorities to look into potential dangers in the working environment. Authorities are now threatening with fines if the companies don't follow the regulations.

- Eivind Reiten, head of the Norsk Hydro ASA aluminium division, says Hydro Aluminium may expand abroad because of limited power supply in Norway and the advantage of a strategic position towards customers.
- Norwegian bond rates could fall if the central bank eases controls of money market rates, senior economist Terje Furunes at Union Bank of Norway says.
- In spite of tougher competition both abroad and amongst, Norwegian broker companies are doing very well.

- Norwegian computer companies want to ease the strict regulation on immigration in order to employ Russian programmers. Managing director in Episteme, Inge Simon Thorbjoernsen, says Russian programmers are better and cheaper than Norwegians.
